summary: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table, even when nothing matches on the right.
points: The table after FROM is the left table, and the table after LEFT JOIN is the right.
When nothing matches, the right table's columns are NULL.
To count matches, use COUNT(right_column), not COUNT(*), so unmatched rows count as 0.
Choose the left table by asking which rows must all appear.

example.sql:
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
example.explanation: Noor stays in the result with 0 orders, which an inner join would have lost.
